title: Unconditional cohomology finiteness across a dense open
statement: Let k be algebraically closed, f:X -> Spec k a reduced curve [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], Λ a finite commutative ring, and F a constructible etale sheaf of Λ-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. For a dense open j:U -> X let G=j_!j^*F [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. All cohomology groups of F are finite if and only if all cohomology groups of G are finite; cohomology is that of the underlying abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. No prime annihilator or properness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof: the finite stalk product, five-term exact sequence, and remarks (a) and (b)

proof.text: Form the reduced closed complement using the vanishing ideal of U complement. Its subscheme inclusion has range complementary to the range of U inclusion. Apply shortExact_openClosedShortComplex to the module sheaf F, then the source library shortExact_map_forget2 to obtain the short exact sequence S of underlying abelian sheaves with S.X1 = j_!j^*F, S.X2 = F, and S.X3 = i_*i^*F.
Apply the closed-boundary cohomology theorem. H^0(S.X3) is finite; each positive H^q(S.X3) is a singleton and therefore finite. Thus all cohomology of the third term is finite.

For an exact pair of additive homomorphisms A -> B -> C with A and C finite, the kernel of the second map equals the image of the first; AddGroup.fintypeOfKerEqRange gives finiteness of B. If all H^q(F) are finite, the initial cohomology map embeds H^0(G) in H^0(F), so H^0(G) is finite. For each q, exactness of H^q(S.X3) -> H^(q+1)(G) -> H^(q+1)(F) and the finite outer terms gives finiteness of H^(q+1)(G).

Conversely, if all H^q(G) are finite, exactness of H^q(G) -> H^q(F) -> H^q(S.X3) gives finiteness of H^q(F) for each q by the same finite-middle-group argument. The proof uses no separately chosen higher-degree isomorphisms and works also for an empty scheme or boundary.
